title: Regression Spotlight: Issue Atlas and Short-term Playbook (Mar 21-22 2026)
summary: Biweekly snapshot focused on newly observed regressions post-onboarding for rw-instruct variants. Highlights overall drift metrics, clustered failure modes, concrete short-term remediations and owners for the next two sprints. Intended audience: applied-ml triage, runtime, and product owners.
content:
Overview:
This 'Issue Atlas' captures the set of top regressions surfaced by the onboarding evals run between 2026-03-14 and 2026-03-21. Data sources: nightly eval harness (onboard-evals), production sampling (hosted-api/route: chat-synth), and promptset fuzz tests. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — prioritized fixes, repro notes, and concrete experiments.

High-level metrics (delta vs baseline model: redwood-v2-large-instruct@2026-03-07):
- Mean correctness (task-specific): -4.6 percentage points
- Hallucination rate (entity hallucinations per 1k tokens): +1.9
- Formatting regressions (expected structured JSON outputs failing schema): +12% failures
- Latency p95: +30ms (no SLA impact, but correlates with longer sequences that trigger KV cache misses)

Top failure clusters (ranked by impact and frequency):
1) Structured-output schema drift
   - Symptom: models generate extra fields or omit required keys for instruction templates (notably invoice/receipt parsers).
   - Example prompt: "Extract {date, total, vendor} from text -> JSON"
   - Observed across rw-instruct-14b-q4_0 and rwd-v2-instruct-7b
   - Probable cause: recent prompt chaining change (PR #442) altered conditioning length and template tokens
   - Short repro: see linked artifact github.com/redwood/repro/issue-112

2) Numeric rounding/precision regressions
   - Symptom: arithmetic transforms return imprecise decimals; failing downstream asserts in CFG scoring.
   - Example: "Compute discount and return total with 2 decimal places"
   - Hit rate higher on quantized variants (q4_0) at long context
   - Mitigation idea: prompt-level post-process normalization or strict float-formatting function call

3) Safety false positives on benign prompts
   - Symptom: model flags innocuous customer support text as policy-violating (false positive safety classifier trigger)
   - Downstream effect: user messages suppressed in staging
   - Links: JIRA ML-4390 includes sample inputs causing trigger

4) Long-prefix hallucination in code completion
   - Symptom: after long setup text (>1024 tokens), the model confidently invents helper functions with wrong signatures
   - Observed p50 drop in exact match for code tasks

5) Stop-token misfires in streaming
   - Symptom: streaming outputs cut off mid-sentence more often for redwood-v2-large-fp16-ctl
   - Correlates with throughput throttling events and modified EOS heuristics in runtime v0.12.3

Repro notes (quick):
- Eval harness command used:
  python -m evals.run --suite onboarding-basic --model rw-instruct-14b-q4_0 --seed 42 --promptset path/to/promptset-v3.yaml
- Repro cluster: ci-onboard-eval-03 (k8s), tag: onboard-2026-03-21
- Quick checks: compare tokenization between model variants (mismatch observed in bpe-v2 vs bpe-v3)

Immediate action items (owners + target dates):
- A1: Roll back prompt-chaining PR #442 for canary to confirm effect (owner: Ethan Liu) — target: 2026-03-24
- A2: Add strict JSON schema post-validate step in evaluator to catch structured-output drift earlier (owner: Priya Raman) — target: 2026-03-25
- A3: Enable float-normalizer postprocess for numeric tasks in onboarding promptset (owner: Mateo Silva) — target: 2026-03-26
- A4: Safety classifier: add sample set from ML-4390 to retrain queue and run near-term threshold adjustment (+monitor) (owner: Zoe Park) — target: 2026-04-01
- A5: Streaming EOS heuristics: runtime/serving to run controlled experiment with modified eos_threshold=0.92 (owner: SRE-ticket assigned: SRE-781) — target: 2026-03-29

Short experiments to run (if A1 confirms regression):
- E1: Prompt template hardening: move required-keys into a single anchored prefix token to reduce conditioning variance
- E2: Quantization sanity: run small-batch eval comparing q4_0 vs q8_0 across numeric tasks to isolate rounding shifts
- E3: Tokenization audit: convert small promptset to bpe-v3 to test whether token boundary differences explain schema drift

Open questions / unresolved:
- How much of the structured-output drift is due to runtime batching vs content-conditioning? (needs A/B with runtime 0.12.2)
- Is the hallucination increase concentrated on a subset of prompt templates or broadly spread across categories?
- Can we implement a lightweight 'schema-aware' decoding penalty quickly in the runtime to reduce invalid JSON outputs?

Blocking items:
- Need a canary slot for rollback (capacity booking) — POC with Dedicated infra team required
- Safety retrain dataset requires legal sign-off for some redacted support logs

Suggested communications:
- Short email to product owners summarizing major user impact (formatting & hallucinations) — target send 2026-03-23
- Slack #applied-ml pinned message with top-3 repros + how to run local eval (owner: Priya)

Next sync:
- Triage huddle: 2026-03-24 10:00 PT (30m) — agenda: confirm whether rollback A1 changes signal, pick two experiments to run.
- Weekly status note to broader eng: 2026-03-27

Appendix (quick links and artifacts):
- Eval harness: github.com/redwood/evals/tree/main/onboard-harness
- Repro notebook: github.com/redwood/repro/blob/main/onboard-issue-atlas.ipynb
- Live dashboard: internal.redwood.com/dashboards/onboard-regressions (read-only)

Notes-to-self:
- prioritize structured-output fix if rollback confirms cause; it's the highest customer-visible failure
- keep numeric normalizer narrow-scoped to onboarding evals only; don't change runtime globally without more tests
